target.title: refactor(qa): simplify transport adapter contracts
target.body:
Fixes #99622

## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab needs one asynchronous owner boundary for constructing QA Channel and Crabline adapters, but method support should come from the adapter implementation itself. Parallel declarations duplicated the adapter interface and could drift from the methods available on a selected channel.

Crabline Telegram supports native-command injection and outbound preview-sequence observation. Crabline Slack does not. The transport contract now represents that difference directly: channel-specific methods are optional, and an attempted flow call fails clearly at the invocation point when the selected adapter does not implement the method.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change keeps an injectable asynchronous adapter factory registry while simplifying the transport contract:

- `QaTransportAdapterFactory` retains `id`, `matches`, and asynchronous `create`.
- The registry retains default QA Channel and Crabline factories and supports injected custom factories.
- Registry creation returns adapter-owned cleanup.
- Factory selection and startup errors include the factory, driver, and channel context.
- Channel-specific methods are optional and exist only on adapters that implement them.
- Scenario runtime bindings use the adapter and its state directly instead of a second alias surface.
- QA Channel, Crabline, suite, manual-lane, and self-check creation use the same asynchronous registry path.

The change remains inside the QA Lab plugin boundary. It does not change production channel behavior.

## User Impact

No direct end-user behavior changes. QA maintainers and channel contributors get a smaller transport contract, one extensible asynchronous construction boundary, deterministic cleanup ownership, and clear failures when a scenario invokes a method unavailable on the selected channel.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/qa-transport-registry.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-flow-runner.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-runtime-api.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/qa-channel-transport.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-flow.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/manual-lane.runtime.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/self-check.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite.test.ts` — 9 files, 86 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "observes Telegram preview edits through the shared transport adapter|configures OpenClaw's Slack plugin against a Crabline local provider server"` — 2 tests passed, 13 skipped.
- Repository `oxfmt`, scoped `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwmvq9cz6xp5nnnvm9917ev0` — `check:changed` passed with full project typecheck, all oxlint shards, import-cycle validation, and changed guards. Actions run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28682699653
- Codex autoreview — clean, no accepted/actionable findings; correctness confidence 0.89.
